cues.en: Before we dive into deep learning, there are a few algorithms you need to understand first, as they are important concepts of how deep learning works.
cues.zh: 深入深度學習之前，先了解幾個演算法，因為它們是深度學習運作的重要概念。

cues.en: One of these pre-requisites is stochastic gradient descent, or SGD - that's the same SGD we talked about when we covered matrix factorization.
cues.zh: 其中一個先備知識，是隨機梯度下降，簡稱 SGD，也就是矩陣分解時談過的同一個 SGD。

cues.en: As I mentioned, it's possible to implement matrix factorization using neural networks, so it shouldn't come as any surprise that you can train both approaches using the same technique.
cues.zh: 如前所述，矩陣分解可以用神經網路實作，因此兩種方法能用相同技術訓練，並不意外。

cues.en: We're also going to talk about autodiff, which is a mathematical trick that SGD depends on with neural networks.
cues.zh: 也會談自動微分，也就是 autodiff，這是神經網路中 SGD 仰賴的數學技巧。

cues.en: And we'll cover softmax, which is used at the output of neural networks to translate their raw outputs into more useful rating classifications.
cues.zh: 還會介紹 softmax，用在神經網路輸出端，把原始輸出轉成更有用的評分類別。

cues.en: The first thing we want to talk about is gradient descent.
cues.zh: 首先要談的是梯度下降。

cues.en: This is basically a machine learning optimization technique for trying to find the most optimal set of parameters for a given problem.
cues.zh: 它基本上是一種機器學習最佳化技術，試圖為特定問題找出最適合的一組參數。

cues.en: So what we're plotting here is basically some sort of cost function, some measurement of the error of your learning system - this applies to machine learning in general.
cues.zh: 這裡畫的基本上是某種成本函數，也就是衡量學習系統誤差的方式，這適用於一般機器學習。

cues.en: You're going to have some sort of function that defines how close your predicted values are to the actual observed values.
cues.zh: 你會有某種函數，定義預測值與實際觀察值有多接近。

cues.en: So in the context of supervised learning, we will be feeding our algorithm, or model, a group of parameters.
cues.zh: 因此，在監督式學習情境中，會把一組參數給演算法或模型。

cues.en: These parameters define ways that we have tuned the model, and we need to identify different values of those parameters that produce the optimal results.
cues.zh: 這些參數定義我們如何調整模型，需要找出能產生最佳結果的不同參數值。

cues.en: So the idea with gradient descent is that you just pick some point at random, and each one of these dots represents some set of parameters to your model.
cues.zh: 梯度下降的概念是，先隨機選一點，每個點代表模型的某組參數。

cues.en: Maybe it's the various parameters for some model we've talked about before, or maybe it's the exact weights within your neural network.
cues.zh: 也許是前面某種模型的不同參數，也可能是神經網路中的實際權重。

cues.en: Whatever it is, we're going to try some set of parameters to start with, and then we will measure whatever the error that produces on our system.
cues.zh: 不管是什麼，先嘗試一組參數，再衡量它讓系統產生多少誤差。

cues.en: Then, we move on down the curve here.
cues.zh: 接著，沿著曲線往下移動。

cues.en: So we'll try a different set of parameters here, again, just like moving in a given direction with different parameter values, and then we measure the error that we get from that,
cues.zh: 在這裡試另一組參數，也就是朝某個方向改變參數值，再衡量產生的誤差，

cues.en: and in this case we actually achieved less error by trying this new set of parameters.
cues.zh: 這次，新參數的誤差確實比較少。

cues.en: So we say, "Okay, I think we're "heading in the right direction here.
cues.zh: 於是說：「好，我想方向是對的。

cues.en: "Let's change them even more in the same way," and we just keep on doing this at different steps until we finally hit the bottom of a curve here and our error starts to increase after that point.
cues.zh: 繼續用相同方式改更多。」就這樣一步一步，直到到達曲線底部，超過那個點之後，誤差開始增加。

cues.en: So at that point we'll know that we've actually hit the bottom of this gradient - and that's the nature of the term here, gradient descent.
cues.zh: 那時就知道，確實到了這個梯度的底部，這就是「梯度下降」這個詞的意義。

cues.en: Basically we're picking some point at random with a given set of parameters that we measure the error for, and we keep on pushing those parameters in a given direction until the error minimizes itself
cues.zh: 基本上，隨機選一點，對某組參數衡量誤差，持續朝某個方向推動參數，直到誤差最小，

cues.en: and starts to come back up some other value.
cues.zh: 然後又開始回升。

cues.en: And that's how gradient descent works in a nutshell.
cues.zh: 這就是梯度下降的概要。

cues.en: I'm not going to get into all the hard core mathematics of it all; the concept is what's important here because gradient descent is how we actually train our neural networks to find an optimal solution.
cues.zh: 不會深入所有艱深數學，這裡重要的是概念，因為梯度下降是實際訓練神經網路，找出最佳解的方法。

cues.en: Now you can see there are some areas of improvement here for this idea.
cues.zh: 現在可以看到，這個想法有一些可改善之處。

cues.en: First of all, you can actually think of this as sort of a ball rolling downhill, so one optimization that we'll talk about later is using the concept of momentum.
cues.zh: 首先，可以把它想成球往山下滾，因此稍後會談到一種最佳化方式，利用動量概念。

cues.en: You can actually have that ball gain speed as it goes down the hill here, and slow down as it reaches the bottom.
cues.zh: 球往下滾時可以加速，接近底部時再減速。

cues.en: That's the way to make it converge more quickly when you're doing things and can make the actual training of your neural networks even faster.
cues.zh: 這讓它更快收斂，也讓神經網路實際訓練更快。

cues.en: Another thing we're talking about is the concept of local minima.
cues.zh: 另一件要談的事，是局部最小值。

cues.en: So what if I randomly picked a point that ended up over on this curve here?
cues.zh: 如果隨機選的起點，落在這裡的曲線上，會怎樣？

cues.en: I might end up settling into this minima here which isn't actually the point of the least error.
cues.zh: 可能停在這個最小值，但它其實不是誤差最低的位置。

cues.en: The point with the least error on this graph is over here to the right.
cues.zh: 圖中誤差最低的位置，在右邊這裡。

cues.en: That's a general problem with gradient descent.
cues.zh: 這是梯度下降的一般問題。

cues.en: How do you make sure that you don't get stuck in what's called a local minima?
cues.zh: 如何確保不會卡在所謂的局部最小值？

cues.en: Because if you just look at this part of the graph, that looks like the optimal solution, and if I just happen to start over here that's where I'm going to get stuck.
cues.zh: 因為只看這段圖，它似乎就是最佳解；如果剛好從這裡開始，就會卡住。

cues.en: There are various ways of dealing with this problem.
cues.zh: 有很多處理方式。

cues.en: Obviously you could start from different locations, to try to prevent that sort of a thing, but in practical terms it turns out that local minima aren't really that big of a deal when it comes to training neural networks.
cues.zh: 顯然，可以從不同位置開始，試著避免；但實務上，訓練神經網路時，局部最小值其實沒那麼嚴重。

cues.en: This just doesn't really happen that often; you don't end up with shapes like this in practice, so we can get away with not worrying about it too much.
cues.zh: 這種情況不常發生，實務上通常不會得到這種形狀，因此不必太擔心。

cues.en: That's a very good thing, because for a long time people believed that AI would be limited by this local minima effect, but in practice it's really not that big of a deal.
cues.zh: 這是好事，因為很長一段時間，人們以為 AI 會受到局部最小值限制，但實務上，問題真的沒那麼大。

cues.en: Another concept we need to familiarize yourself with something called autodiff.
cues.zh: 另一個需要熟悉的概念，叫做自動微分。

cues.en: We don't really need to go into the hard core mathematics of how autodiff works, you just need to know what it is and why it's important.
cues.zh: 不必深入自動微分的艱深數學，只要知道它是什麼，以及為什麼重要。

cues.en: So when you're doing gradient descent, somehow you need to know what the gradient is, right?
cues.zh: 做梯度下降時，總得知道梯度是多少，對吧？

cues.en: So we need to measure what is the slope that we're taking along our cost function, and to do that mathematically you need to get into calculus, right?
cues.zh: 因此，要衡量沿著成本函數移動時的斜率，數學上就得用到微積分，對吧？

cues.en: If you're trying to find the slope of a curve and you're dealing with multiple parameters, then we're talking about computing partial derivatives, which sounds pretty intense.
cues.zh: 要找曲線斜率，又涉及多個參數，就需要計算偏導數，聽起來很難。

cues.en: The first partial derivatives figure out the slope that we're heading in.
cues.zh: 一階偏導數，能找出前進方向上的斜率。

cues.en: It turns out that this is very mathematically intensive and inefficient for computers to do, so taking a brute force approach to gradient descent turns out to be very hard to do.
cues.zh: 這在數學上非常繁重，電腦處理也沒效率，因此用暴力方法做梯度下降，很難。

cues.en: Autodiff is a technique for speeding that up.
cues.zh: 自動微分就是加速的方法。

cues.en: Specifically we use something called reverse-mode autodiff.
cues.zh: 具體來說，使用反向模式自動微分。

cues.en: What you need to know is that it can compute all the partial derivatives you need just by traversing your graph as many times as you have outputs plus one.
cues.zh: 你只要知道，它只需走訪計算圖「輸出數加一」次，就能算出所需的所有偏導數。

cues.en: This works out really well in neural networks because in a neural network you tend to have artificial neurons that have very many inputs, but probably only one output, or very few outputs in comparison to the inputs.
cues.zh: 這在神經網路特別有效，因為人工神經元通常有很多輸入，但大概只有一個輸出，或相較之下很少的輸出。

cues.en: So this turns out to be a pretty good little calculus trick.
cues.zh: 所以這是相當不錯的微積分技巧。

cues.en: It's complicated - look up the details if you really want to get into the hardcore math behind it - but it works.
cues.zh: 它很複雜，真的想深入艱深數學，可以查細節，但它確實有效。

cues.en: Autodiff is what the TensorFlow library uses under the hood to implement its gradient descent.
cues.zh: TensorFlow 函式庫內部，就是用自動微分實作梯度下降。

cues.en: You're never going to have to actually implement gradient descent from scratch or implement autodiff from scratch; these are all baked into the libraries that we're using such as TensorFlow.
cues.zh: 你不必從零實作梯度下降或自動微分，它們都已內建在 TensorFlow 等函式庫中。

cues.en: But they are terms that we throw around a lot, so it's important that you at least know what they are and why they're important.
cues.zh: 但這些詞會經常出現，所以至少知道它們是什麼、為什麼重要。

cues.en: So to review, gradient descent is the technique we're using to find the local minima of the error that we're trying to optimize for, given a certain set of parameters.
cues.zh: 回顧一下，梯度下降是在給定一組參數時，找出想最佳化誤差的局部最小值的技術。

cues.en: Autodiff is a way of accelerating that process, so we don't have to do quite as much math or quite as much computation to actually measure that gradient of the gradient descent.
cues.zh: 自動微分則加速這個過程，減少實際衡量梯度下降中的梯度，所需的數學與運算。

cues.en: One other thing we need to talk about is softmax.
cues.zh: 還有一件要談的是 softmax。

cues.en: The mathematics aren't so complicated here, but again, what's really important is understanding what it is and what it's for.
cues.zh: 這裡的數學沒那麼複雜，但同樣，重要的是了解它是什麼、做什麼用。

cues.en: When you have the end result of a neural network, you end up with a bunch of what we call weights that come out of the neural network at the end.
cues.zh: 神經網路的最終結果，會得到一組我們稱為權重的輸出。

cues.en: So how do we make use of those final weights?
cues.zh: 那麼，怎麼使用這些最終權重？

cues.en: How do we make practical use of the output of our neural networks?
cues.zh: 如何實際運用神經網路輸出？

cues.en: Well, that's where softmax comes in.
cues.zh: 這就是 softmax 的用途。

cues.en: Basically it converts each of the final weights that come out of your neural network into a probability.
cues.zh: 基本上，它把神經網路的每個最終輸出權重，轉成機率。

cues.en: So if you're trying to classify something in your neural network like, for example, deciding if an image is a picture of a face or a picture of a dog or a picture of a stop sign,
cues.zh: 如果神經網路要做分類，例如判斷影像是人臉、狗，還是停車標誌，

cues.en: you might use softmax at the end to convert those final outputs of the neurons into probabilities for each class.
cues.zh: 最後可以用 softmax，把神經元的最終輸出，轉成每個類別的機率。

cues.en: Then you can just pick the class that has the highest probability.
cues.zh: 接著，選機率最高的類別即可。

cues.en: So it's just a way of normalizing things into a comparable range and in such a manner that if you actually choose the highest value of the softmax function from various outputs, you end up with the best choice
cues.zh: 所以，它只是把數值正規化到可比較的範圍，讓你從不同輸出中，選擇 softmax 最高值時，最後得到最佳的

cues.en: of classification at the end of the day.
cues.zh: 分類選擇。

cues.en: It's just a way of converting the final output of your neural network into an actual answer for a classification problem.
cues.zh: 就是把神經網路的最終輸出，轉成分類問題實際答案的方法。

cues.en: So again, you might have the example of a neural network that's trying to drive your car for you, and it needs to identify pictures of stop signs or yield signs or traffic lights.
cues.zh: 再次舉例，神經網路可能要替你開車，需要識別停車標誌、讓路標誌或紅綠燈的圖片。

cues.en: You might use softmax at the end of some neural network that will take your image and classify it as one of those sign types.
cues.zh: 可以在某個神經網路最後使用 softmax，接受影像，將它分類為其中一種標誌。

cues.en: So again, just to recap: gradient descent is an algorithm for minimizing error over multiple steps.
cues.zh: 再次回顧，梯度下降是一種透過多個步驟，將誤差最小化的演算法。

cues.en: Basically, we start with some random set of parameters, measure the error, move those parameters in a given direction, see if that results in more error or less error and just try to move in the direction
cues.zh: 基本上，從某組隨機參數開始，衡量誤差，朝某個方向移動參數，看看誤差增加還是減少，再試著往

cues.en: of minimizing error until we find the actual bottom of the curve.
cues.zh: 讓誤差最小的方向前進，直到找到曲線真正的底部。

cues.en: That point is where we have a set of parameters that minimizes the error of whatever it is you're trying to do.
cues.zh: 那個位置，就是讓目標工作誤差最小的一組參數。

cues.en: Autodiff is just a calculus trick for making gradient descent faster; it makes it easier to find the gradients in gradient descent just by using some calculus trickery.
cues.zh: 自動微分只是讓梯度下降更快的微積分技巧，利用一些微積分方法，讓尋找梯度更容易。

cues.en: Softmax is just something we apply on top of our neural network at the very end to convert the final output of our neural network to an actual choice of classification given several classification types to choose from.
cues.zh: Softmax 是最後套用在神經網路上的東西，將最終輸出，轉成多種候選分類中的實際選擇。

cues.en: So those are the basic mathematical terms or algorithmic terms that you need to understand to talk about artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 以上就是討論人工神經網路，需要了解的基本數學與演算法用語。

cues.en: With that under our belt, let's talk about artificial neural networks next.
cues.zh: 具備這些知識後，接著談人工神經網路。
